readme.logo: Chess Trainer logo: four board squares with C, T, a pen and a clock
readme.intro: Opening trainer you run on your own computer: a bot plays your repertoire, Stockfish takes over when theory ends, and every game is saved to review. Real clocks, Chess960, PGN, Chess.com and Lichess import. Multilingual. Docker or desktop app, no accounts. It runs on Linux, Windows and macOS (amd64 or arm64), with no internet needed to play.
readme.reviewed: Only US English, Brazilian Portuguese and Latin American Spanish are reviewed. Every other language, English (UK) included, is machine-made and unreviewed. Corrections are welcome. Open a [Translation fix issue]({fix}).
readme.run.title: Run
readme.run.image: Or, without cloning, run the published image (amd64 or arm64); your games stay in `./data`:
readme.run.network: The app is published on loopback only, because it has no login. To reach it from another device, set `CHESS_TRAINER_BIND=0.0.0.0`, on a network you trust, and list the names you will open it by in `CHESS_TRAINER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (such as `192.168.0.10,chess.lan`): the app answers only to `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` otherwise. `CHESS_TRAINER_PORT` changes the port.
readme.run.desktop: **Desktop app (preview):** the same app in its own window, without Docker, for Windows, macOS and Linux. To download and install it, see [{install}]({install}); how it is built is in [desktop/](desktop/README.md). Docker stays the reference way to run it.
readme.how.title: How it works
readme.how.guide: The full guide, with pictures, is in [{help}]({help}), the same as the Help screen in the app, and who made it and why is in [{about}]({about}). A summary:
readme.how.pick: Pick your color and the lines to drill, from all 3,865 lines of the book. Search by name, ECO or moves. Each selected line has the same chance of being drawn.
readme.how.bot: The bot plays the drawn line. If you play a move from another selected line, it follows you.
readme.how.deviation: A move outside the selected lines is a deviation: it is recorded with the expected moves and shown at the end of the game.
readme.how.engine: When the line ends or someone leaves theory, Stockfish takes over at the selected level.
readme.how.hide: Unchecking "Show moves" hides the move list and the opening name, headings included, during a game, so you can write on paper. They come back at the end.
readme.beyond.title: Beyond openings:
readme.beyond.clocks: **Clocks:** bullet, and the blitz, rapid and classical presets of a DGT 3000 clock, or no clock.
readme.beyond.chess960: **Chess960:** roll one of the 960 starting positions, or paste its FEN, and play Stockfish.
readme.beyond.saved: **Saved games:** every game is saved. Filter them, export them as PGN, review them move by move, or start a new game from any of their moves (not yet from a Chess960 game).
readme.beyond.import: **Import:** paste PGN, upload a file, or fetch a player's public games from Chess.com or Lichess. The review shows the PGN's evaluations, classifications, clocks, comments and side lines.
readme.beyond.eval: **Evaluation bar:** Stockfish's evaluation while reviewing, and at the end of a game. It is a quick check, not a full analysis: for that, export the PGN to Chess.com or Lichess.
readme.beyond.sheet: **Scoresheet:** a printable A4 scoresheet, modeled on an official one, to write your moves by hand during long games. It is not an official scoresheet: it is for training only.
readme.beyond.help: **Help:** how to use every screen, in the app's menu.
readme.fairPlay: Chess Trainer is for training. Never use it, or any engine, during a game against another person.
readme.state: **Current state:** the book and games are in DuckDB (`data/chess-trainer.duckdb`). Bot levels are provisional. The UI is in {count} languages. See the [project brief](docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md) for what comes next.
readme.book.title: The book
readme.book.text: The bot's book is in `openings/`, one JSON file per opening family, loaded into DuckDB on start (a few seconds the first time). It starts with all 3,865 lines of the [Lichess openings catalog](https://github.com/lichess-org/chess-openings). Any line plays with either color. The catalog lists named positions, not recommended replies, so lines are often short and the engine plays on from there. They can be extended by pull request, recording the source. The format is in [the brief, §6](docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md).
readme.book.data: The database lives in `./data`, which the container writes as UID 1000. To back it up, stop the app and copy the file. Every move is saved there, so an unfinished game continues when you open the page again, even after a restart. Clocks stop while the app is closed.

readme.develop.title: Develop
readme.develop.needs: Needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Test commands and conventions are in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md), and how to contribute in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
readme.develop.session: To work with an AI coding assistant, start the session with the prompt in [docs/SESSION_PROMPT.md](docs/SESSION_PROMPT.md).
readme.develop.pictures: The pictures in Help are screenshots of the app in each language. After a visible UI change, make them again against a running app (it plays and resigns games):

install.title: How to install Chess Trainer
install.intro: Chess Trainer is a free program that runs on your own computer. It needs no account and no internet to play. These steps take about five minutes.
install.download.title: 1. Download
install.download.text: Open the [Releases page](https://github.com/nielsencampos/chess-trainer/releases/latest) and, under **Assets**, download the file for your computer:
install.download.macArm: Mac with an Apple chip (M1, M2, M3…), macOS 11 Big Sur or newer
install.download.macIntel: Mac with an Intel processor, macOS 11 Big Sur or newer
install.download.needs: **What you need:** any computer from this century. If it has an HDMI port and no tube monitor, it will run. To be exact: one of the systems above, 64-bit, and a screen of at least 1280x720.
install.download.whichMac: Not sure which Mac you have? Open the Apple menu → **About This Mac**. "Chip: Apple M…" means Apple chip; "Processor: Intel" means Intel.
install.download.size: The download is about 100 to 300 MB, because it includes the Stockfish chess engine.
install.open.title: 2. Install and open
install.windows.smartscreen: Windows may show **"Windows protected your PC"** (SmartScreen). It appears because the program is new and not signed by a paid certificate, not because something is wrong with it. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
install.windows.installer: Follow the installer. It needs no administrator password, and it adds **Chess Trainer** to the Start menu (and to the desktop, if you tick that box).
install.windows.open: Open **Chess Trainer** from the Start menu.
install.windows.webview: If the window stays blank, install the free **Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime** from Microsoft's website (Windows 11 and up-to-date Windows 10 already have it).
install.windows.zip: **Without installing:** the `chess-trainer-…-windows-x64.zip` file holds the same program. Right-click it → **Extract All…**, then open **chess-trainer.exe** in the extracted folder. If it says *Failed to execute script 'launcher'*, delete the extracted folder, right-click the zip → **Properties** → tick **Unblock** → **OK**, and extract it again.
install.mac.unzip: Double-click the zip file in your Downloads folder (Safari may have unzipped it already). You get **Chess Trainer**.
install.mac.first: Double-click it. The first time, macOS says it cannot verify the app, because it is not notarized by Apple (that needs a paid developer account). To open it anyway:
install.mac.sequoia: **macOS 15 Sequoia or newer:** click **Done**. Open **System Settings** → **Privacy & Security**, scroll down to the message about "Chess Trainer" and click **Open Anyway**. Enter your password, then click **Open Anyway** again.
install.mac.sonoma: **macOS 14 Sonoma or older:** Control-click (or right-click) **Chess Trainer** in Applications → **Open** → **Open**.
install.mac.remembers: macOS remembers your choice; from then on it opens normally.
install.mac.damaged: If macOS says the app **"is damaged and can't be opened"**, open the **Terminal** app and paste this line, then press Return and open the app again:
install.linux.unpack: Unpack the file: double-click it in your file manager and extract it, or run `tar xzf chess-trainer-*-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`. You get a `chess-trainer` folder.
install.linux.terminal: In a terminal, inside that folder, run:
install.linux.copies: It copies the program to `~/.local/opt/chess-trainer` and adds **Chess Trainer** to your applications menu. It needs no administrator password.
install.linux.open: Open **Chess Trainer** from the applications menu. You can also run `./chess-trainer` from the folder without installing.
install.linux.x11: If the window does not open on an X11 desktop, install the `libxcb-cursor0` package (for example `sudo apt install libxcb-cursor0`).
install.data.title: Where your games and lines are kept
install.data.text: Your saved games, imported games and your lines are in one file, `chess-trainer.duckdb`, in this folder. The folder also holds the log (`chess-trainer.log`) and the screen preferences (theme, language, board) in `webview`.
install.data.windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\chess-trainer` (paste it in the File Explorer address bar)
install.data.apart: The program and your data are kept apart: installing a new version or removing the program does not touch your games.
install.backup.title: Back up
install.backup.close: Close Chess Trainer. While it is open, recent changes are still in a separate `chess-trainer.duckdb.wal` file, and a copy of the database alone would miss them.
install.backup.copy: Copy the whole `chess-trainer` folder above to a USB drive, a cloud folder or another disk.
install.backup.restore: To restore, close Chess Trainer and put the folder back in the same place. The database file works on any system, so you can also use it to move your games to another computer. A database from the Docker version (`data/chess-trainer.duckdb`) can be copied in the same way.
install.update.title: Update
install.update.text: Download the new version and install it the same way, replacing the old program (Windows: run the new installer; macOS: replace the app in Applications; Linux: run `./install.sh` from the new folder). Your games stay where they are.
install.uninstall.title: Uninstall
install.uninstall.windows: **Windows:** **Settings** → **Apps** → **Installed apps** → **Chess Trainer** → **Uninstall**. If you used the zip instead, delete its folder.
install.uninstall.mac: **macOS:** drag **Chess Trainer** from Applications to the Trash.
install.uninstall.data: Only if you also want to erase your games and lines: delete the data folder listed above. This cannot be undone, so make a backup first if you may want them later.
install.trouble.title: If something goes wrong
install.trouble.one: Open only one Chess Trainer at a time.
install.trouble.port: Chess Trainer uses port 47800 on your own computer. If another program uses it, Chess Trainer does not start; the reason is written in `chess-trainer.log` in the data folder.
install.trouble.report: To report a problem, open an [issue](https://github.com/nielsencampos/chess-trainer/issues) and attach `chess-trainer.log`.
install.docker.title: The other way: Docker
install.docker.text: If you already use Docker, you can run the same app without installing it: see [Run in the README]({run}). It opens in your browser at <http://127.0.0.1:8000> and keeps its data in the `data/` folder of the project.
